QF.id: Issue Management - General Obligations and Due Diligence_52

question.text: A company is making a Further Public Offer (FPO) of Rs. 300 crore. Using the proposed-issue-size basis, what is the minimum promoter contribution required?

explanation.text: The Logic: For an FPO, the source allows the minimum promoter contribution to be calculated as either 20% of the proposed issue size or 20% of the post-issue capital. Using the proposed-issue-size basis specified in the stem, 20% of Rs. 300 crore = Rs. 60 crore. The Trap: Rs. 75 crore (25% of the issue size) is tempting for candidates who misremember the percentage. Rs. 100 crore is a distractor based on a different concept (the Rs. 100 crore threshold rule) and does not apply here. Note: When solving FPO promoter-contribution problems, identify which basis the question intends — proposed issue size or post-issue capital — because the source rule is either-or, not fixed to one basis.
